questions.question: What are the four main parts of an article?
options: Headline, introduction/lead, body, conclusion
Greeting, body, sign-off, PS
Title, characters, plot, moral
Question, hypothesis, method, results
questions.explanation: An article has a headline, an introduction (lead), a body with subheadings, and a conclusion.

questions.question: What are the 5 Ws that a good article lead often answers?
options: Who, What, Where, When, Why
Wish, Want, Will, Would, Was
Write, Watch, Wait, Walk, Win
Weather, Water, Wind, Waves, Warmth
questions.explanation: The lead (ingress) should quickly answer Who, What, Where, When and Why to give the reader the essentials.

questions.question: What makes a good headline?
options: It is short, catchy and informative
It is at least 20 words long
It hides what the article is about
It is written entirely in lowercase letters
questions.explanation: A good headline is short, attention-grabbing and tells the reader what the article is about.

questions.question: How should you use a direct quote in an article?
options: Put the exact words in quotation marks and say who said them
Change the words but keep the quotation marks
Never name the person you quote
Use quotes instead of writing any text yourself
questions.explanation: A direct quote reproduces the exact words in quotation marks with the source named, e.g.: "Reading changed my life," says teacher Anna Berg.

questions.question: What is the purpose of subheadings in the body of an article?
options: To organise the text so each section covers one aspect of the topic
To make the article look longer
To replace the headline
To hide the conclusion
questions.explanation: Subheadings break the body into clear sections, each dealing with one aspect, making the article easier to navigate and read.
